title: dedicated-autoscaler: improve burst controls and per-fleet utilization reporting
author: Aisha Khan
description: Motivation: Dedicated customers requested stronger guarantees around short-term burst throughput while preventing noisy tenants from starving steady-state capacity. We also need better per-fleet utilization visibility to explain burst behavior in billing and SLO dashboards. This PR implements: 1) new burst token bucket controller per-fleet with configurable burst_quota and recharge_rate; 2) admission policy that prioritizes reserved-capacity reservations and applies soft throttles for best-effort workloads during sustained overloads; 3) per-fleet utilization reporting pipeline that emits 1m/5m rolling metrics (utilization_pct, burst_consumed, burst_available) to the observability backend and to the Dedicated billing export; 4) autoscaler integration that uses burst headroom signals to avoid aggressive downscales immediately after large bursts. Changes are backward-compatible by default: new fleet config fields have sensible defaults that preserve current behavior. Migration notes: existing dedicated fleets will inherit default burst limits (burst_quota=10k_tokens, recharge_rate=500_tokens/min) until operators explicitly tune them. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked (ENG-1842) - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] staging canary on 3 fleets - [x] observability dashboards updated - [x] release notes drafted - [x] rollforward plan prepared Testing: added extensive unit tests for token bucket logic, e2e integration test that injects synthetic traffic patterns to verify throttle behavior and autoscaler stability; ran canary on staging and two customer-sim fleets for 48h. Observability: new metrics are prefixed dedicated.fleet.* and available in console under "Dedicated -> Fleet Utilization". Rollout: feature gated behind cluster feature-flag dedicated_burst_v2 and enabled by default for internal fleets, staged to customers over two weeks. Monitoring/alerts: added SLO guardrails to detect misconfigured infinite recharge_rate and abnormal burst drain patterns. Performance: microbenchmarks show token admission adds <0.5ms median to request path when cache-hot and negligible p95 impact. Deployment: squash-merged to main and rolled to canary; no config migration required. Refer to files_changed for a summary of touched modules and to review_comments for discussion history.

release_notes: Improved dedicated fleet burst controls: added configurable token-bucket based burst quota and recharge rate, per-fleet utilization metrics exposed in console and billing exports, and autoscaler integration to prevent downscales immediately after heavy bursts. Default settings preserve existing behavior; operators can tune per-fleet settings. See docs/releases/dedicated-burst-v2.md for details and dashboards.
rollout_notes: Gate is dedicated_burst_v2. Internal fleets enabled immediately; external customer enablement via console toggle and Linear task ENG-2010 to coordinate support. Staged rollout: 10% of fleets week 1, 50% week 2, 100% week 3 if no regressions. Canary results stored in CI artifacts.
impact_summary: Provides stronger short-term throughput guarantees for reserved capacity, clearer billing/observability for burst consumption, and reduces autoscaler churn after bursts. Adds minimal request-path latency (<0.5ms median).
